title: Single-cell RNA-seq reveals immune cell heterogeneity and increased Th17 cells in human fibrotic skin diseases
creator: Cheng-Cheng Deng, Xue-Yan Xu, Yan Zhang, Long-Can Liu, Xuan Wang, Jun-Yi Chen, Liu-Yi Yao, Ding-Heng Zhu, Bin Yang
description: BackgroundFibrotic skin disease represents a major global healthcare burden, characterized by fibroblast hyperproliferation and excessive accumulation of extracellular matrix components. The immune cells are postulated to exert a pivotal role in the development of fibrotic skin disease. Single-cell RNA sequencing has been used to explore the composition and functionality of immune cells present in fibrotic skin diseases.

title: Patient preferences for treatment‑free intervals in multiple myeloma: mixed‑methods insights on monitoring trade‑offs and supportive care improvements
creator: Anna Fleischer, Mohammad Barakat, Jessica Peter, Sofie-Katrin Kadel, Christine Riedhammer, Patrick-Pascal Strunz, Julia Mersi, Johannes Waldschmidt, K Martin Kortüm, Hermann Einsele, Imad Maatouk, Leo Rasche
description: PurposeContinuous and maintenance therapy remains central to multiple myeloma (MM) care, but repeated treatment-related healthcare encounters may impose physical, psychosocial, and logistical burden. We explored patient preferences regarding intervals between active treatment contacts, monitoring trade-offs, and opportunities to improve inpatient and outpatient care.MethodsA 12-month, single-center mixed-methods survey was conducted among 100 patients with MM at a German tertiary center.

title: Assessment of accuracy and efficiency of guided fixation of customized 3D miniplates vs Champy’s technique in stabilization of mandibular angle fractures: A randomized controlled trial
creator: Arwa Hosni, Mohamed Shawky, Mohamed Ibrahim Sakr, Waleed El-Beialy, Mostafa Ezz, Mohammed Atef
description: ObjectivesThe objectives of this study were; (1) to assess the accuracy of virtual surgical planning (VSP) and computer aided design and manufacturing (CAD/CAM) in creating an anatomically oriented, bone-borne fracture reduction/plate positioning patient specific surgical guide (PSSG) and a customized three-dimensional (3D) miniplate to achieve anatomical reduction and stabilization of fractured segments in mandibular angle fractures (MAF) via a more

title: Long-chain organic molecules enable mixed dimensional perovskite photovoltaics: a brief view
creator: Xianfang Zhou, Taomiao Wang, Xiao Liang, Fei Wang, Yan Xu, Haoran Lin, Ruiyuan Hu, Hanlin Hu
description: The remarkable optoelectronic properties of organometal halide perovskite solar cells have captivated significant attention in the energy sector. Nevertheless, the instability of 3D perovskites, despite their extensive study and attainment of high-power conversion efficiency, remains a substantial obstacle in advancing PSCs for practical applications and eventual commercialization.

title: Early transcriptomic changes at the skin interface during Powassan virus transmission by Ixodes scapularis ticks
creator: Dakota N. Paine, Meghan Hermance, Saravanan Thangamani
description: IntroductionPowassan virus (POWV), a vector-borne pathogen transmitted by Ixodes ticks in North America, is the causative agent of Powassan encephalitis. As obligate hematophagous organisms, ticks transmit pathogens like POWV at the tick bite site, specifically during the initial stages of feeding. Tick feeding and salivary factors modulate the host’s immunological responses, facilitating blood feeding and pathogen transmission.

title: A dual-electropolymerized poly(Xylenol orange)@poly(Euchrysine) sensing interface for sustainable simultaneous electroanalysis of 5-fluorouracil and empagliflozin: density functional theory mechanistic elucidation
creator: Rania S. Ibrahim, Hanaa M. Abd El-Wadood, Marwa R. El-Zahry, Antonio Frontera, Noha M. Hosny
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). A sensitive and sustainable electroanalytical approach for the simultaneous determination of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) and empagliflozin (EMPA) is desirable for pharmaceutical and bioanalytical investigations, particularly in preliminary studies exploring their concomitant use and potential protective effects. Herein, a square-wave voltammetric (SWV) method was developed using a sequentially fabricated poly-XO@poly-EUC/PGE sensing interface, prepared by successive electropolymerization of euchrysine (EUC) and xylenol orange (XO) on the surface of pencil graphite electrode (PGE). Electrochemical and morphological characterization confirmed successful electrode modification and improved interfacial electron-transfer properties.

title: Association between oral ulcerative lesions, oral infections, and fever during the pre-engraftment phase after hematopoietic cell transplantation: results from the Orastem study
creator: A. M. G. A. Laheij, J. E. Raber-Durlacher, B. Hasséus, M. C. Huysmans, S. J. M. van Leeuwen, K. Garming Legert, J. E. Johansson, S. Isom, D. M. Kline, M. D. Hazenberg, F. R. Rozema, M. T. Brennan, I. von Bültzingslöwen, N. M. A. Blijlevens
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeThe percentage of cases with fever of unknown origin after hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) is high. An often overlooked clinical infection in HCT recipients may be chronic inflammation from the oral cavity.

title: Network modeling of problematic social media use components in college student social media users
creator: Jianyong Chen, Ting Su, Junqiang Dong, Yuzhi Li, Ju Feng, Yingxiu Chen, Gu Liu
description: BackgroundWhile the constitutive features of problematic social media use (PSMU) have been formulated, there has been a lack of studies in the field examining the structure of relationships among PSMU components.MethodThis study employed network analytic methods to investigate the connectivity among PSMU components in a large sample of 1,136 college student social media users (M age = 19.

title: Occupational needle stick injuries in a tertiary ophthalmic care setup: An eastern India perspective
creator: Prerana Vijay, Sujata Das, Srikant Kumar Sahu, Bibhusita Samal, Kirteemayee Sarangi, Smruti Rekha Priyadarshini
description: 17% of work-related accidents.[1] The adoption of advanced microsurgical techniques in ophthalmology has increased the risk of sharp injuries, especially when instrument handling occurs under high magnification and low lighting conditions.[23] This primarily occurs while operating, disposal and recapping of sharp instruments, improper handling, cleaning, and administering injections.

title: Synonymous variants in the ATP6AP2 gene may lead to developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
creator: Yan Liang, Lin Wan, Huimin Yan, Xinting Liu, Jing Zhang, Gang Zhu, Guang Yang
description: ObjectiveTo the literature, variants in the ATP6AP2 gene may cause abnormal nervous system development and associated neurological symptoms.MethodsWe report a patient with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) carrying an ATP6AP2 c.858G > A (p.Ala286=) synonymous variant. In addition, an overview of reported patients with the same variant were collected and summarized to compare our findings.

title: Context‐dependent effects of whole‐body vibration on reproductive function and penile tissue integrity in sedentary male rats
creator: Mujdat Ayva, Senay Akin, Irem Gungor Orhan, Neslihan Coskun Akcay, Berkay Ozerklig, Kemal Kosemehmetoglu, Mesut Altan, Haydar A. Demirel, Fazil Tuncay Aki
description: Sedentary behaviour is increasingly recognized as a risk factor for systemic disorders; however, its effects on male reproductive health and penile tissue integrity remain insufficiently understood. Furthermore, the therapeutic role of whole‐body vibration (WBV) has not been investigated. This study evaluated the effects of sedentary behaviour on testicular and penile tissues and examined whether WBV could attenuate these alterations.

title: Spatial multi-omics identifies an SPP1+ macrophage-driven anti-apoptotic niche in osteoarthritis synovium via the SPP1-CD44 axis
creator: Han Gong, Hao Shen, Feng Zhang, Wei Wang, Sheng Zhou, Lei Wang, Yu Sun
description: Osteoarthritis (OA) progression is driven by chronic synovitis. However, the spatially organized macrophage subsets that sustain unresolved inflammation through evasion of apoptosis remain poorly characterized. The present study investigated the functional subsets and spatial niches of synovial macrophages that regulate apoptotic pathways in OA pathogenesis.

title: Hippocampal ΔFosB expression is associated with cognitive impairment in a subgroup of patients with childhood epilepsies
creator: Chia-Hsuan Fu, Jason C. You, Carrie Mohila, Robert A. Rissman, Daniel Yoshor, Angela N. Viaene, Jeannie Chin
description: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder characterized by recurrent seizures, and is often comorbid with other neurological and neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD). Patients with recurrent seizures often present with cognitive impairment. However, it is unclear how seizures, even when infrequent, produce long-lasting deficits in cognition.

title: PINK1 promotes the progression of lung squamous cell carcinoma through the FAK/AKT/RhoA/vinculin pathway
creator: Xu Li, Yuhui Ma
description: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) is an aggressive malignancy with a poor prognosis. Given the association between mitochondrial dysregulation and LUSC, the aim of the present study was to identify mitochondrial unfolded protein response (UPRmt)-related candidate genes associated with LUSC and to explore their potential functional relevance.

title: Improved plant biomass production under low nitrogen conditions through conditional accumulation of the second messenger, guanosine tetraphosphate, in chloroplasts and mitochondria
creator: Mina Goto, Takanari Nemoto, Kazuma Sakoda, Atsushi Sakurai, Sousuke Imamura, Shinji Masuda
description: To enhance plant biomass production under low nitrogen conditions, we employed a method to artificially and temporarily accumulate the bacterial second messenger, guanosine tetraphosphate (ppGpp), to modify plastidial or mitochondrial metabolism. Specifically, we fused a chloroplast or mitochondrial transit-peptide to the N-terminus of the bacterial ppGpp synthase YjbM, which was conditionally expressed by an estrogen-inducible promoter in Arabidopsis.

title: Measuring the Outcomes of International Oncology Regulatory Collaboration in Canada from 2019 to 2025: Project Orbis
creator: Jonathan Zaslavsky, David C Sealey
description: Project Orbis, launched by the US FDA in 2019, enables collaboration among international regulatory agencies on cancer drug reviews. We assessed the regulatory impact of Project Orbis in Canada by analyzing publicly available data on marketing authorization applications (MAAs). We analyzed US‐Canada submission and approval gaps, time to regulatory decision, tumor areas, and sponsor involvement.

title: Exploring the association between caffeine intake and benign prostatic hyperplasia: results from the NHANES 2005–2008
creator: Fei Zhang, Andong Zhang, Junyue Tao, Meng Zhang, Chaozhao Liang
description: BackgroundCoffee is a physiologically active food component prevalent throughout the world, but the association between caffeine intake and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) has been limited in extensive epidemiological studies.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study to evaluate the association between caffeine intake and BPH in adults in the United States using data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2005–2008.

title: Thyrotoxicosis-Associated Cholestatic Jaundice in a Patient With Incidental Gallstone Disease: A Case Report and Literature Review
creator: Zakaria Yahya Khawaji, Basim Saleh Samman, Basem Younis Alturkistany, Hatim Mahmoud, Yousef Mohammed Alalawi
description: Patient: Female, 62-year-old Final Diagnosis: Hyperthyroidism Symptoms: Abdominal pain • jaundice • tachycardia • weight loss Clinical Procedure: — Specialty: Endocrinology and metabolic Objective: Unusual clinical course BackgroundThyrotoxicosis is associated with well-recognized and clinically significant complications, including congestive heart failure and cardiac arrhythmias.

title: Timing of umbilical cord clamping and its predictors among neonates in Northeast Ethiopia: a multicenter prospective observational study
creator: Zenebe Tefera, Mandefro Assefaw, Lemlem Chanyalew Melese, Molla Kassa, Abdulkadir Kassaw, Nigusie Abebaw, Atrsaw Dessie Liyew, Mengistu Abate Belay
description: BackgroundOptimal umbilical cord clamping, defined as clamping between one and three minutes after birth, is recommended by the World Health Organization to improve infant health and nutritional outcomes through placental transfusion. Despite these recommendations, early cord clamping remains prevalent in many settings, depriving neonates of up to 30% greater blood volume and increasing the risk of iron deficiency anemia.

title: Clopidogrel combined with rivaroxaban in peripheral artery disease after revascularization
creator: Min Lu, Jiaqi Li, Huanyu Ni, Tong Qiao, Baoyan Wang
description: BackgroundTo evaluate the efficacy and safety of clopidogrel-rivaroxaban combination compared to aspirin-rivaroxaban combination in patients with symptomatic peripheral artery disease (PAD).MethodsConsecutive patients with symptomatic PAD patients were analyzed from January, 2018 to June, 2022 at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital. Patients were divided into two groups based on the antithrombotic therapy.

title: High-grade synovitis associates with clinical markers and response to therapy in chronic inflammatory arthritis: post hoc analysis of a synovial biomarkers prospective cohort study
creator: Carlo Garaffoni, Marianna Tamussin, Ilaria Calciolari, Giovanni Lanza, Alessandra Bortoluzzi, Carlo Alberto Scirè, Marcello Govoni, Ettore Silvagni
description: BackgroundInflammatory arthritis (IAs), such as rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and psoriatic arthritis (PsA), are characterized by the presence of chronic synovitis. The Krenn’s synovitis score (KSS), a simple tool detectable by haematoxylin/eosin staining of synovial biopsy samples, allows the discrimination between high-grade and low-grade synovitis.

title: Vascular calcification: pathogenic mechanisms, signaling crosstalk and translational therapeutics
creator: Rui Hua, Bao Qiao, Xuehao Liu, Bingchen Jiang, Jinlei Wu, Chuanxin Zhang, Han Liu, Bailu Wang, Shujian Wei, Yuguo Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Vascular calcification (VC) is a multifactorial pathological process characterized by ectopic deposition of hydroxyapatite in the arterial wall, which is closely associated with increased cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of current insights into the pathogenesis of VC, emphasizing its nature as a dynamically regulated process driven by intricate crosstalk among diverse molecular mechanisms, signaling cascades, and pathological pathways. Under specific pathological stimuli, this intricate regulatory network disrupts the homeostatic balance between pro-calcific and anti-calcific mechanisms.

title: Altered cortical activation patterns in post-stroke patients during walking with two-channel functional electrical stimulation: a functional near-infrared spectroscopy observational study
creator: Sheng Xu, Shizhe Zhu, Minyao Li, Tianjiao Zhang, Qinglei Wang, Youxin Sui, Ying Shen, Kan Chaojie, Ren Zhuang, Chuan Guo, Tong Wang, Lan Zhu
description: Restoration of independent walking ability is the primary objective of stroke rehabilitation; however, not all patients achieve this goal due to diverse impairments in the paretic lower limb and compensatory mechanisms that lead to an asymmetrical and mechanically inefficient gait.

title: Urban Habitat Mosaics Structure Gene Flow but Preserve Genetic Diversity in an Invasive Termite
creator: Emilie Gheyle, Edouard Duquesne, Yves Roisin, Denis Fournier
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Urbanization is expanding rapidly in tropical regions, yet its effects on the genetic structure and connectivity of invasive social insects remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how urban and forest habitat contexts are associated with genetic diversity, population structure, and colony organization in the invasive termite Heterotermes tenuis (Hagen, 1858) across three paired urban‐forest sites in Guadeloupe, using 18 newly developed polymorphic microsatellite loci. A total of 414 workers from 50 nests were genotyped.

title: Patterns and Environmental Drivers of Amphibian Alpha and Beta Diversity in the Huangshan Mountains, Southern Anhui, China
creator: Suyue Wang, Ziyi Wang, Yujia Sun, Zhirong He, Qingyan Sun, Jiedong Wei, Yingxin Li, Meiting Liu, Jiayi Shi, Chunna Zhang, Siyu Wu, Yufeng Bai, Ziruo Zhang, Na Zhao, Supen Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Understanding the spatial patterns of biodiversity and their environmental determinants is fundamental to ecology and conservation, particularly in mountainous transitional zones where species assemblages can shift rapidly. Amphibians, as highly sensitive organisms, are excellent indicators of environmental change, yet quantitative assessments of their diversity in the Huangshan Mountains—a biodiversity hotspot at the junction of the Palaearctic and Oriental realms in southern Anhui, China—remain limited.

title: Posterior root repair with high tibial osteotomy improves radiological and clinical outcomes despite greater medial meniscus extrusion: A comparison of transtibial and all‐inside techniques
creator: Yuki Fujie, Kazunori Yasuda, Koji Yabuuchi, Taku Ebata, Masayuki Inoue, Norimasa Iwasaki, Eiji Kondo
description: PurposeTo evaluate whether the transtibial pullout (TTP) or all‐inside suture (AIS) technique provides superior radiological and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing medial meniscus posterior root (MMPR) repair combined with high tibial osteotomy (HTO) over a 24‐ to 48‐month follow‐up.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study analysed 54 knees in 52 patients who underwent MMPR repair with HTO between April 2018 and March 2022.

title: Severe ARDS due to disseminated toxoplasmosis in a person with HIV successfully treated with ECMO: a case report
creator: Daniel Medina, Renzo Ávila, Graciela Rodríguez-Sevilla, Víctor Gumucio, María Bonilla, Gabriela Abelenda-Alonso, Jordi Niubó, Maria Saumoy, Juan Tiraboschi, María Paz Fuset, Arkaitz Imaz
description: Disseminated toxoplasmosis (DT) is an uncommon but severe complication associated with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). This case report describes the successful treatment of a 28-year-old male individual with AIDS who developed severe and life-threatening acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) resulting from DT, in which extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) was employed effectively.

title: Antibody-based sensing of pesticide residues and mycotoxins in plant-derived foods: A narrative review of ELISA, lateral-flow immunoassays and immunosensors
creator: Harsh Kumar, Shivani Guleria, Lukas Peter, Nahid Akhtar, Rabia Asghar, Hasnita Binti Che Harun, Dinesh Kumar, Kamil Kuča, Ayaz Mukarram Shaikh, Endre Harsányi, Béla Kovács
description: Cereals and their products, as well as fruits and vegetables, form a major constituent of the human diet worldwide. These food items can become contaminated with mycotoxins during farming, transportation, or storage. They are exposed to pesticides mostly during cultivation and also during storage and transportation, where pesticides are applied to prevent pest infestation.

title: Plant–microorganism–soil interaction under long-term low-dose ionizing radiation
creator: Guoqiang Zeng, Yingzi Wen, Chuyang Luo, Yihong Zhang, Fei Li, Chao Xiong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). As the environmental nuclear radiation pollution caused by nuclear-contaminated water discharge and other factors intensifies, more plant–microorganism–soil systems will be under long-term low-dose ionizing radiation (LLR). However, the regulatory mechanisms of the plant–microorganism–soil system under LLR are still unclear. In this study, we study a system that has been stably exposed to low-dose ionizing radiation for 10 years and investigate the response of the plant–microorganism–soil system to LLR based on the decay of the absorbed dose rate with distance.

title: Peripheral Nerve Stimulation Reduces Opioid Use and Facilitates Early Ambulation Following Fibular Flap Harvest: A Retrospective Study
creator: Kyu J. Choi, Alexander Ivan B. Posis, Alane Costanzo, Anthony Scherschel, Jesse R. Qualliotine, Yan T. Ortiz-Pomales, Eamon O’Reilly, Daniel A. Hammer
description: Background:Fibular free flap (FFF) reconstruction is the gold standard for mandibular and maxillary defects, but donor-site pain remains challenging. Multimodal analgesia (MMA) relies on opioids, which risk dependence, systemic side effects, and delayed recovery. Regional nerve blocks reduce pain but have inconsistent efficacy owing to variable drug metabolism, potential effects on flap perfusion, and motor blockade.

title: Description of the vaginal microbiota in nulliparous ewes during natural mating and pregnancy: preliminary signs of the male preputial microbiota modulation
creator: Marta Barba, Marion Toquet, Empar García-Roselló, Jesús Gomis, Juan J. Quereda, Pedro González-Torres, Belén Carbonetto, Ángel Gómez-Martín
description: The vaginal microbiota plays a key role in animals’ health. Understanding its diversity and composition and associated changes occurring through the reproductive cycle represents valuable knowledge to disclose the mechanisms leading to dysbiosis and eventually to infection. Even if the human vaginal microbiota has been thoroughly studied, scarce research has been conducted on the vaginal microbiota of livestock.

title: Design, synthesis, and apoptotic antiproliferative action of new benzimidazole/1,2,3-triazole hybrids as EGFR inhibitors
creator: Alshimaa A. Y. Ahmed, Anber F. Mohammed, Zainab M. Almarhoon, Stefan Bräse, Bahaa G. M. Youssif
description: IntroductionThis work outlines the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a new series of benzimidazole/1,2,3-triazole hybrids as apoptotic antiproliferative agents that inhibit the EGFR pathway.MethodsThe research assesses the antiproliferative efficacy of compounds 6a-i and 10a-i against various cancer cell lines.

title: eNeuro Assessments: A Standardized Way to Communicate Research Quality
creator: Mihaela D. Iordanova
description: or) influence research visibility, commanding the attention of scientists across disciplines and attract interest from policymakers, journalists, and the public. Publication in such journals signals that a paper is significant, with the potential to shape future research. As a result, journal reputation has become a widely used proxy for research quality; shaping careers, funding, and research directions (McKiernan et al.

title: Microneedling Combined With Biomimetic Peptides for Burn Scar Improvement: A Prospective Study
creator: Francisco Hernández Gómez Crespo, Noury Adel, Miguel Rubio Henaine, Karen Dominguez Marchan, Francisco Llano, Diego Ivan Briseno Torres, Jesus Alejandro Lopez-Lara, Gabriela Yareli Zavala Resendiz, Ricardo Villaseñor Domínguez, Cintia Peña Pandura, Alexander Nguyen, Jesper Thulesen, Ida Vega Thulese
description: Background:Hypertrophic scarring commonly follows burn injury, resulting from persistent inflammation, abnormal fibroblast activity, and excessive extracellular matrix deposition, leading to functional limitation and aesthetic impairment. Despite multimodal management, outcomes remain variable. Biomimetic peptides can modulate cellular pathways involved in tissue repair, whereas microneedling enhances transdermal delivery and stimulates dermal remodeling.

title: Dough Rheology, Physico‐Chemical, and Sensory Properties of Bread From Wheat/Fresh Green Mature Banana Puree Composite
creator: Ediriisa Mugampoza, Norah Nankya, Arthur Tabula, Martin Mutambuka, Khadijah Nakyinsige
description: Wondering whether fresh green mature bananas could be used for supplementation of resistant starch and dietary fiber in bakery products, our study set out to evaluate the effect of partial substitution of wheat flour with different forms of banana (fresh whole fingers, fresh pulp, whole finger flour, and pulp flour) on dough rheology, physico‐chemical and sensory properties of bread.

title: Potential roles of Culicoides spp. (Culicoides imicola, Culicoides oxystoma) as biological vectors of bluetongue virus in Yuanyang of Yunnan, P. R. China
creator: Nan Li, Jinxin Meng, Yuwen He, Wenhua Wang, Jinglin Wang
description: Introduction Culicoides plays a crucial role as an insect vector in the field of veterinary medicine. The transmission of significant viruses such as bluetongue virus (BTV) and African horse sickness virus (AHSV) by this insect poses a substantial threat, leading to the development of severe diseases in domestic animals.

title: Outcomes and Complications of Monobloc Versus Le Fort III Procedures for Treating Craniosynostosis: A Literature Review
creator: Bassem Chamma, Suhas Nagappala, Mitchell Arnold, Sara Trumza, Kirollos Samir Tadrousse, Sahil Kapur, Mark Houdi, Richard Simman
description: Background:Craniosynostosis is a congenital disorder resulting in the early fusion of several bones in the skull, causing a deformity of the head and facial structures. The 2 most commonly performed surgical procedures to treat craniosynostosis include the monobloc and Le Fort III procedures.

title: Loss of control eating in children is associated with altered cortical and subcortical brain structure
creator: Alaina L. Pearce, Bari Fuchs, Shana Adise, Travis D. Masterson, Nicole Fearnbach, Laural English, Kathleen L. Keller
description: IntroductionLoss of control (LOC) eating is the perceived inability to control how much is eaten, regardless of actual amount consumed. Childhood LOC-eating is a risk factor for the development of binge-eating disorder (BED), but its neurobiological basis is poorly understood. Studies in children with BED have shown both increased gray matter volume in regions related to top-down cognitive control (e.g.

title: Effects of partial replacement of soybean meal with Chlorella vulgaris and lysozyme on diarrheal incidence, plasma biochemical parameters, and immunity of weaned piglets
creator: Md. Abul Kalam Azad, Bowen Li, Ting Ye, Binghua Qin, Qian Zhu, Yordan Martinez, Xiangfeng Kong
description: IntroductionThe study aimed to investigate the effects of Chlorella vulgaris and lysozyme on growth performance, diarrhea rate, immune function, plasma biochemical parameters, and gut microbiota and metabolites of weaned piglets.MethodsThirty weaned Xiangcun black piglets (BW, 11.47 ± 1.13 kg) were randomly assigned to one of three treatment groups: corn-soybean meal-based basal diet (CON group), soybean meal replaced with 5% C.

title: Effect of short video addiction on the sleep quality of college students: chain intermediary effects of physical activity and procrastination behavior
creator: Zhe Zhao, Yali Kou
description: IntroductionThe purpose of this study was to examine the impact of short video addiction on college students' sleep quality and to elucidate the mechanism underlying this relationship. Thus, we examined the correlation between short video addiction and sleep quality and analyzed the roles of physical activity and procrastination.

title: A Sensitive LC–MS/MS Method for Quantifying Beta‐Casomorphin 5 in Pasteurized Milk
creator: Duc Doan Nguyen, Vicky Solah, Suzanne Daubney, Malgorzata Kowalczyk, Wendy Hunt
description: This study aimed to apply a highly sensitive liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) method to quantify beta‐casomorphin 5 (β‐CM5) content in pasteurized milk (PM) and to evaluate the effect of heat treatment on this peptide. Commercial PM samples were collected from local supermarkets, and heat treatment of industrial milk (IP) samples was performed at 62°C and 72°C for 5 min.

title: AIP56, an AB toxin secreted by Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida, has tropism for myeloid cells
creator: Inês Lua Freitas, Maria Fátima Macedo, Liliana Oliveira, Pedro Oliveira, Ana do Vale, Nuno M.S. dos Santos
description: IntroductionThe AB-type toxin AIP56 is a key virulence factor of Photobacterium damselae subsp. piscicida (Phdp), inducing apoptosis in fish immune cells. The discovery of AIP56-like and AIP56-related toxins in diverse organisms, including human-associated Vibrio strains, highlights the evolutionary conservation of this toxin family, suggesting that AIP56 and its homologs may share conserved receptors across species.

title: Newly diagnosed and relapsed follicular lymphoma: EHA Clinical Practice Guidelines for diagnosis, treatment, and follow‐up
creator: Marco Ladetto, Natacha Bolaños, Guy Bouguet, Klaus Herfarth, Wolfram Klapper, Sirpa Leppa, Kim Linton, Armando Lopez‐Guillermo, Stefano Luminari, Franck Morschhauser, Jessica Okosun, Ewa Paszkiewicz‐Kozik, Catherine Thieblemont, Sanne Helene Tonino, Marek Trneny, Judith Trotman, Umut Yilmaz, Martin
description: Follicular lymphoma (FL) is the second most common lymphoma subtype in Europe, with a median age at diagnosis of 60–65 years. It is generally considered an indolent disease, and the median overall survival at diagnosis now likely exceeds 20 years. However, considerable heterogeneity exists. Diagnosis requires adequate biopsy material and a specialized hematopathologist.

title: Discordant Cavitary Changes: A Radiological Dilemma in Invasive Mucinous Adenocarcinoma: A Case Report
creator: Akina Nigi, Noritaka Miya, Keisuke Iwamoto, Hidetoshi Itani, Shigeto Kondou
description: Treatment‐related cavitary transformation in lung cancer may complicate radiological response assessment. We report a man in his 70s with stage IVA invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma treated with atezolizumab, bevacizumab, carboplatin and paclitaxel. After two cycles, CT showed enlargement of cavitary components despite regression of solid tumour components, making response assessment difficult.

title: Proteomics and transcriptomics combined reveal specific immunological markers in autoimmune thyroid disease
creator: Xia Chen, Hui Chen
description: ObjectiveThe pathogenesis of AITD remains unclear to date. This study employs a combination of proteomics and transcriptomics analysis to identify and validate specific immune response markers in patients with hyperthyroidism and hypothyroidism, thereby providing a scientific basis for the clinical diagnosis and treatment of AITD.

title: A Case of Platypnea‐Orthodeoxia Syndrome Caused by Patent Foramen Ovale, Accompanied by Dilated Ascending Aorta, Thoracic Kyphosis and Persistent Eustachian Valve
creator: Ayaka Kishimoto, Tomohiro Namiki, Yudai Ogata, Hiroya Sunabe, Toshihide Inui, Hiroaki Ishikawa, Hiroko Watanabe, Chihiro Ohta, Ruriko Numata, Naoto Kawamatsu, Tomoko Machino‐Ohtsuka, Tomoya Hoshi, Tohru Sakamoto
description: We present a case of platypnea‐orthodeoxia syndrome (POS) associated with patent foramen ovale (PFO). In the upright position, right atrial compression resulting from a dilated ascending aorta and thoracic kyphosis modifies the spatial alignment of the PFO, orienting it toward inferior vena cava (IVC) inflow and increasing its tendency to remain patent.

title: Global, national, and regional burden of acute myeloid leukemia among 60–89 years-old individuals: insights from a study covering the period 1990 to 2019
creator: Pengyin Chen, Xinling Liu, Yao Zhao, Yuyuan Hu, Jiaxin Guo, Haiying Wang
description: BackgroundOur study examined the global, national, and regional trends in the incidence, mortality, and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) associated with older people’s acute myeloid leukemia (AML) over a 30 years period. AML, which predominantly affects individuals aged 60–89, is known for its severity and unfavorable prognosis.

title: Effects of aging-related muscle degeneration on dynamic stability during walking: a musculoskeletal computer simulation study
creator: Shoma Kudo, Masahiro Fujimoto, Akinori Nagano
description: IntroductionAging-related deficits in the physiological properties of skeletal muscles limit the control of dynamic stability during walking. However, the specific causal relationships between these factors remain unclear. This study evaluated the effects of aging-related deficits in muscle properties on dynamic stability during walking.MethodsWalking movements were simulated using two-dimensional musculoskeletal models consisting of 18 Hill-type muscles.

title: Mental health and Multiracial/ethnic adults in the United States: a mixed methods participatory action investigation
creator: Jaimie Shaff, Xinzi Wang, Janel Cubbage, Sachini Bandara, Holly C. Wilcox
description: IntroductionAddressing gaps in the integration of justice, diversity, equity, and inclusion (J-DEI) in public health research and practice, this study investigates the mental health of Multiracial and multiethnic adults in the United States (U.S.). A rapidly growing racial/ethnic group in the U.S.

title: Analysis of artery injury types and clinical characteristics of patients with transcatheter angioembolization after percutaneous nephrolithotomy
creator: Xianghu Meng, Rong Cong, Yibo Hua, Zengjun Wang, Ninghong Song, Wei Yang, Rijin Song
description: BackgroundThere is no systematic classification of renal vascular injuries conducted for severe post-percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) bleeding.AimThe aim of the present study was to explore the various types of artery injury and clinical characteristics of patients who underwent transcatheter angioembolization (TAE) after PCNL.

title: Adverse events in paediatric spinal deformity surgery – 12-year review of specialist spinal deformity practice
creator: Edward J Bayley, Shreya Srinivas, Matthew Bellamy, Adya Ranjan, Dominic M Luttrell, Michael Athanassacopoulos, Anthony L R Michael, Lee M Breakwell, Ashley A Cole
description: AimsAdverse events following paediatric spinal deformity surgery in the UK suffers from significant reporting gaps, as current data relies predominantly on voluntary incident submissions. This retrospective study aims to comprehensively assess the incidence of all surgical adverse events at a specialized paediatric spinal orthopaedic centre.

title: Assessing inflammation and predicting relapse in ulcerative colitis is more accurate when performed by IBD specialized gastroenterologists
creator: Madeline Alizadeh, Lauren A George, Ameer Abutaleb, Wenqing Cao, Bruce D Greenwald, Harris T Feldman, Shien Hu, David Hudesman, Frances Onyimba, Suparna Sarkar, Kristen Stashek, Katherine Sun, Uni Wong, Samantha Zullow, Jordan Axelrad, Raymond K Cross
description: BackgroundUlcerative colitis is monitored through clinical, laboratory, endoscopic, and histologic measures. Persistence of histologic inflammation despite clinical and endoscopic remission is associated with disease flare.MethodsWe compared the identification of clinically significant histologic inflammation by general and IBD-specialized gastroenterologists (GI) using a simplified binary scoring system and looked at associations with disease relapse.

title: The gut microbiome and cross-reactivity of food allergens: current understanding, insights, and future directions
creator: Carolina Taico Oliva, Ibrahim Musa, Daniel Kopulos, Fariba Ardalani, Anish Maskey, Aaron Wilson, Nan Yang, Xiu-Min Li
description: This mini-review examines the emerging role of the gut microbiome in influencing food allergen cross-reactivity. It specifically focuses on how microbial diversity, antigens, and metabolites impact IgE-mediated allergic responses. Cross-reactivity occurs when structurally similar food and microbial antigens trigger hypersensitivities, affecting millions of people worldwide. Recent research underscores the significance of microbial diversity in early life for developing immune tolerance.

title: Correction to: Real-world Effectiveness of Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 Vaccine in Preventing RSV-associated Lower Respiratory Tract Disease Hospitalization in Adults ≥60 Years of Age: Early Results From a Test-negative Design Analysis
creator: Unknown
description: , David Singer, Elizabeth M La, Andrew G Allmon, Dominique Luyts, Hung-Fu Tseng, Real-world Effectiveness of Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 Vaccine in Preventing RSV-associated Lower Respiratory Tract Disease Hospitalization in Adults ≥60 Years of Age: Early Results From a Test-negative Design Analysis, Open Forum Infectious Diseases, Volume 13, Issue 5, May 2026, ofag279, https://doi.org/10.

title: Retained Colorectal Foreign Body After Suspected Chemical Incapacitation: A Surgical and Forensic Challenge
creator: Rohan Karkra, Kenneth R. Wilhalme, Sameer Rao, Ethan Shamsian, Vraj Shah, Edwin Teehan, Sima Vossough‐Teehan
description: Retained rectal foreign bodies are an uncommon but clinically significant surgical emergency. We report the case of a 74‐year‐old male with multiple medical comorbidities who presented with progressive rectal pain and obstipation several days after an episode of suspected drug‐facilitated assault.

title: Facing emotions: real-time fMRI-based neurofeedback using dynamic emotional faces to modulate amygdala activity
creator: Apurva Watve, Amelie Haugg, Nada Frei, Yury Koush, David Willinger, Annette Beatrix Bruehl, Philipp Stämpfli, Frank Scharnowski, Ronald Sladky
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionMaladaptive functioning of the amygdala has been associated with impaired emotion regulation in affective disorders. Recent advances in real-time fMRI neurofeedback have successfully demonstrated the modulation of amygdala activity in healthy and psychiatric populations.

title: Association between different insulin resistance indices and all-cause mortality in patients with diabetic kidney disease: a prospective cohort study
creator: Huan Zhu, Yinmei Chen, Dexin Ding, Hui Chen
description: AimPrevious research has shown a strong association between insulin resistance (IR) and both the onset and advancement of diabetic kidney disease (DKD). This research focuses on examining the relationship between IR and all-cause mortality in individuals with DKD.MethodsThis study utilized data obtained from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), spanning the years 2001 to 2018.

title: Fully Threaded Versus Partially Threaded Cannulated Screws in the Treatment of Nondisplaced or Valgus-Impacted Geriatric Femoral Neck Fractures: A Retrospective Cohort Study
creator: Mark Ayoub, Samuel Saucedo, Emilio Robles, Yeng Vue, Armen Martirosian
description: Introduction:Partially threaded cannulated screws (PTCS) have been associated with high rates of femoral neck shortening (FNSH) and complications in the treatment of geriatric femoral neck fractures. There are limited studies directly comparing the use of all fully threaded cannulated screws (FTCS) with PTCS. The purpose of this study was to compare outcomes between FTCS versus PTCS.

title: A Systematic Review of Antidiabetic Mechanisms of Passiflora edulis: Beyond Glycemic Control
creator: Luiz Ricardo Teixeira de Farias, Mariáurea Matias Sarandy, Reggiani Vilela Gonçalves, Emanuella de Aragão Tavares, Silvana Maria Zucolotto
description: Passiflora edulis, commonly known as passion fruit, is traditionally used in various cultures for its calming and antidiabetic effects. This systematic review aimed to evaluate the potential of P. edulis on DM based on preclinical evidence from in vivo studies.

title: How Patients' Inquiry Shapes Meaning in Primary Care Consultations: A Qualitative Study Using Own‐Point‐of‐View Video‐Stimulated Recall
creator: Louis‐Baptiste Jaunay, Anne‐Sophie Ivanoff, Corentin Philippot, Emmanuel Triby, Thierry Pelaccia
description: RationaleMedical consultations are collaborative encounters in which physicians and patients jointly address health concerns and make decisions. While most research has focused on physicians' clinical reasoning, decision‐making is increasingly viewed as a form of situated cognition, distributed across individuals and their interactions. However, the patient's perspective on how they make sense of their health problems remains underexamined.

title: An improved U-net and attention mechanism-based model for sugar beet and weed segmentation
creator: Yadong Li, Ruinan Guo, Rujia Li, Rongbiao Ji, Mengyao Wu, Dinghao Chen, Cong Han, Ruilin Han, Yongxiu Liu, Yuwen Ruan, Jianping Yang
description: IntroductionWeeds are a major factor affecting crop yield and quality. Accurate identification and localization of crops and weeds are essential for achieving automated weed management in precision agriculture, especially given the challenges in recognition accuracy and real-time processing in complex field environments.

title: Stroke Caregiver Education and Training in an Inpatient Sub‐Acute Setting: A Retrospective Clinical Audit
creator: Madelaine McCarthy, Nicky Baker, Natasha A Selenitsch, Maayken van den Berg
description: Caregiver burden is a significant issue post‐stroke. Caregivers demonstrate unmet needs throughout the rehabilitation phase, with limited literature that delves into the details of caregiver education and training (CGET) provision prior to discharge.ObjectivesTo identify current practice of multidisciplinary team documentation of CGET following stroke on an inpatient subacute neurosciences ward.

title: The association between controlling nutritional status and postoperative pulmonary complications in patients with colorectal cancer
creator: Yafang Li, Chuang Nie, Na Li, Jieying Liang, Ning Su, Chunhua Yang
description: BackgroundPostoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) significantly impact surgical outcomes, and Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, a simple and easily available nutritional score, has been demonstrated to be significantly associated with postoperative patient outcomes and complications, including PPCs. However, there are few studies that specifically focus on patients undergoing radical surgery for colorectal cancer (CRC).

title: Correction to “Re: “Palliative Care in Europe: Safeguarding Compassion Amidst Changing End‐Of‐Life Policies and Expanding Access to Medically Assisted Dying Position Statement on Behalf of the European Academy of Neurology, the European Federation of Neurological Associations and OneNeurology” by Ru
creator: Unknown
description: ies and Expanding Access to Medically Assisted Dying Position Statement on Behalf of the European Academy of Neurology, the European Federation of Neurological Associations and OneNeurology” by Rukavina Et al,” European Journal of Neurology 33, no. 9 (2026): e70758, 10.1111/ene.70758. The affiliations for Alessandra Solari were incorrect.

title: Activated Clotting Time‐Guided Systemic Heparinization as One Component of a Stepwise Salvage Algorithm for Inadequate Internal Mammary Artery Flow in Microsurgical Breast Reconstruction
creator: Kazuhiro Tsunekawa, Daisuke Yanagisawa, Shunsuke Yuzuriha
description: BackgroundThe internal mammary vessels are commonly used as recipient vessels for free flap breast reconstruction. However, inadequate arterial flow may be encountered intraoperatively. This hypothesis‐generating study evaluated the safety and feasibility of activated clotting time (ACT)‐guided systemic heparinization as one component of a salvage strategy in such situations.

title: Diagnostic Impact of Intracranial Vessel Wall MRI on Ischemic Stroke Etiology in Young Adults
creator: Juhan Reimand, Siim Schneider, Riina Vibo, Liisa Kõrv, Dagmar Loorits, Karl Jõgi, Teele Tuularu, Nele Taba, Kateriine Orav, Janika Kõrv
description: BackgroundIntracranial vessel wall imaging (VWI) enables visualization of arterial wall pathology and may improve etiologic classification of ischemic stroke, but existing evidence is largely based on retrospective studies. We aimed to prospectively evaluate the diagnostic impact of VWI in young stroke patients.

title: Case conceptualization in child welfare: an underused resource to improve child, family, and provider outcomes
creator: Jill R. McTavish, Angela McHolm, Anne Niec, Anna Marie Pietrantonio, Christine McKee, Harriet L. MacMillan
description: Case conceptualization, formally known as case formulation, is one tool that assists in determining the best course of action for children and families experiencing family violence that has been under-utilized in child welfare. In this article we present a step-by-step case conceptualization process that considers the child welfare context.

title: Regionally Divergent Relationships Between Microbial Communities and Environmental Gradients in Potato Production Systems
creator: Shan Shan, Isabelle George, Linda L. Kinkel, Richard A. Lankau
description: Using soil microbiome data as indicators of soil health remains a challenging task in agriculture research. Microbiome data are complex and exhibit strong spatiotemporal variation and diverse responses to environmental factors. As a result, measurements of microbiota often are difficult to interpret and do not provide credible inferences about soil health status.

title: Transdiagnostic clustering of self-schema from self-referential judgements identifies subtypes of healthy personality and depression
creator: Geoffrey Chern-Yee Tan, Ziying Wang, Ethel Siew Ee Tan, Rachel Jing Min Ong, Pei En Ooi, Danan Lee, Nikita Rane, Sheryl Yu Xuan Tey, Si Ying Chua, Nicole Goh, Glynis Weibin Lam, Atlanta Chakraborty, Anthony Khye Loong Yew, Sin Kee Ong, Jin Lin Kee, Xin Ying Lim, Nawal Hashim, Sharon Huixian Lu, Mich
description: IntroductionThe heterogeneity of depressive and anxiety disorders complicates clinical management as it may account for differences in trajectory and treatment response. Self-schemas, which can be determined by Self-Referential Judgements (SRJs), are heterogeneous yet stable. SRJs have been used to characterize personality in the general population and shown to be prognostic in depressive and anxiety disorders.

title: Understanding Chrononutrition for Managing Shift Workers' Health: A Narrative Review and Future Directions
creator: Yan Yin Phoi, Maxine P Bonham, Jillian Dorrian, Michelle Rogers, Alison M Coates
description: Shift workers have temporal eating patterns characterised by irregular food intake and prolonged periods of eating with more energy intake occurring in night‐time hours during night shifts. These patterns of eating against a backdrop of shift work exacerbate circadian misalignment, which impairs cardiometabolic profiles and increases the risk of developing overweight and obesity, diabetes and cardiovascular diseases.

title: CD146 promotes resistance of NSCLC brain metastases to pemetrexed via the NF-κB signaling pathway
creator: Hao Qu, Yan Fang, Feng Zhang, Wenwen Liu, Shengkai Xia, Wenzhe Duan, Kun Zou
description: IntroductionPemetrexed is a first line drug for brain metastases from lung cancer, either as monotherapy or combined with other drugs. The frequent occurrence of initial and acquired resistance to pemetrexed results in limited treatment effectiveness in brain metastases. CD146 was recently found to play important roles in chemoresistance and tumor progression.

title: Cryopreservation of primary neonatal rat oligodendrocytes and recapitulation of in vitro oligodendrocyte characteristics
creator: Hanki Kim, Bum Jun Kim, Seungyon Koh, Hyo Jin Cho, Byung Gon Kim, Jun Young Choi
description: IntroductionIn vitro, primary rat oligodendrocytes (OLs) are widely used for research on OL development, physiology, and pathophysiology in demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis. Primary culture methods for OLs from rats have been developed and improved over time, but there are still multiple aspects in which efficiency can be boosted.

title: What Can Be Learned About Organizational Ethical Blindness When the Wishes of Inpatients in Acute Psychiatric Settings Are Embraced: An Observational Study
creator: Lisbeth Hybholt, Susanne Winkel, Lene Lauge Berring
description: The study explores how the co‐created non‐pharmacological intervention ‘Wishing Well’ may support patient autonomy and recovery‐oriented practice in an acute psychiatric ward. During the ‘Wishing Well’ meetings, inpatients were invited to express concrete wishes for improving daily ward life, which were then discussed collaboratively with peers and staff.

title: Type I interferon upregulates IL-18RAP in neutrophils to enhance chemotaxis and bactericidal activity in autoimmune liver diseases
creator: Wenwen Jin, Xi Su, Lizhi Liu, Shilin Du, Wenting Xiong, Zifei Zhu, Cunyan Li
description: ObjectiveGiven the established association of interleukin-18 (IL-18) and IL-18 receptor accessory protein (IL-18RAP) with autoimmune liver diseases (AILD), while their specific mechanism remains unclear, this study aimed to investigate the expression and functional significance of IL-18RAP in neutrophils from patients with AILD.MethodsThe expression levels of IL-18RAP were determined by quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) and Western blot.

title: Mechanisms of γδ T cell accumulation in visceral adipose tissue with aging
creator: Sujata Mukherjee, Maria E. C. Bruno, Jason Oakes, Gregory S. Hawk, Arnold J. Stromberg, Donald A. Cohen, Marlene E. Starr
description: γδ T cells are resident in visceral adipose tissue (VAT) where they show an age-associated increase in numbers and contribute to local and systemic chronic inflammation. However, regulation of this population and mechanisms for the age-dependent accumulation are not known.

title: Comparative effects of exercise modalities on sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders: A systematic review with pairwise, network, and dose-responsemeta-analyses
creator: Ting Wang, Zhuang Ma, Boao Zhu, Yaqiong Tang
description: BackgroundExercise may improve sleep quality in middle-aged and older adults with sleep disorders, but the comparative effects of different exercise modalities and the dose–response relationship remain unclear.MethodsWe systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to May 2026.

title: Identification and validation of potential biomarkers for atrial fibrillation based on integrated bioinformatics analysis
creator: Fei Tong, Zhijun Sun
description: Background: Globally, the most common form of arrhythmias is atrial fibrillation (AF), which causes severe morbidity, mortality, and socioeconomic burden. The application of machine learning algorithms in combination with weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) can be used to screen genes, therefore, we aimed to screen for potential biomarkers associated with AF development using this integrated bioinformatics approach.

title: Validation and modification of a Chinese smell identification test (CSIT-12) in patients with Parkinson's disease and rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder
creator: Xiao-Niu Liang, Xiao-Yue Wang, Jian-Cai Zhu, Yun-Wei Niu, Cong Fu, Hua-Lan Yang, Jian Wang, Huan Yu, Zuo-Bing Xiao, Yi-Min Sun
description: BackgroundTo enhance olfactory screening for Chinese patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) or rapid-eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) by developing and modifying a Chinese Smell Identification Test 12 (CSIT-12).MethodsIn a discovery cohort, 69 PD patients and 47 healthy controls (HCs) were tested on 24 distinct odors using the Sniffin’ Sticks Screening Test 12 (SSST-12) and CSIT-12.

title: Aging in Autism: An Event‐Related Potentials Study of Auditory Change Detection
creator: Marine Bessé, Shasha Morel‐Kohlmeyer, Emmanuelle Houy‐Durand, Philippe Prévost, Laurie Tuller, Badiâa Bouazzaoui, Laurence Taconnat, Julia Capdeville, Lucie Angel, Marie Gomot
description: Autistic individuals are often thought to exhibit reduced tolerance for change, which may stem from atypicalities in sensory processing, particularly in the detection of environmental changes. Within the predictive coding framework, this intolerance may reflect altered generation and updating internal predictions in response to sensory input, leading to increased prediction errors.

title: Expression of the long noncoding RNA Neat1 in saliva, blood, and ventromedial hypothalamus of pigs exposed to psychosocial stressors
creator: Dane Webster, Luoyang Ding, Song Zhang, Darryl D'Souza, Alan Tilbrook, Katelyn Tomas, Sarah Babington, Kate Plush, Dominique Blache, Archa Fox
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The long noncoding RNA Nuclear Paraspeckle Assembly Transcript 1 (NEAT1) is a master regulator of transcriptional and posttranscriptional changes in stress responses. Here we assessed Neat1 lncRNA expression using quantitative PCR in peripheral biological fluids (saliva and blood) and a brain region that regulates stress and emotion (ventromedial hypothalamus) of 12‐week‐old pigs exposed to chronic (social mixing causing conflict) and acute (restraint) psychosocial challenges. We demonstrated that Neat1 is measurable in pig saliva, blood, and brain samples.

title: Correction to: Control-guided refinement of partially specified Boolean networks: applications to RTK signaling
creator: Unknown
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This error has been corrected. Additionally, the ‘Example’ column in Table 1 contained erroneous characters. Table 1Phenotype related terms.aConceptReal-worldExampleNetworkExampleCharacterProperties of interestPresence of FRS2 tyrosine residue phosphorylationSet of BN variables{FRS2}TraitObservation of propertiesFRS2 tyrosine residue is not phosphorylatedCharacter valuation; alternatively a subspace{FRS2 → 0} ⋆0⋆PhenotypeObservation combinationFRS2 or ERK is phosphorylatedCombination of traits⋆ 1 ⋆ ∪ ⋆ ⋆ 1aThe table explaining the notions of character, trait, and phenotype in the context of real-world concepts in Boolean network models.

title: MiR-4298 and lncKRTAP5-6-3 regulated Cathepsin D expression through ERK-MAPK signaling pathway in chronic UVB-damaged HaCaT cells
creator: Xinling Chen, Feng Zhou, Yao Lin, Yue Xia, Jie Zhang, Wenyi Hou, Yu Sun, Wei Lai, Yue Zheng
description: ObjectiveMiRNAs and lncRNAs are important regulators in the process of skin photoaging. In this study, we investigated the expression changes and interactions between miR4298 and lncKRTAP5-6-3 in chronically UVB-damaged human keratinocyte cell line (HaCaT) cells and explored miR4298-MAPK/ERK signaling pathway-Cathepsin D-lncKRTAP5-6-3 mechanisms in photoaging cells.MethodsHaCaT cells were irradiated with 12 mJ/cm2 UVB once a day for 7 days.

title: Editorial: Dissemination, implementation and uptake of digital and technological interventions in practice
creator: Tom Van Daele, Christiaan Vis, Eva Van Assche, Heleen Riper
description: nd anxiety. In highly controlled research studies, these interventions have a substantial impact, leading to both decreases in participants' symptoms, as well as improvements in their quality of life [e.g. (1)]. Similar effects are also increasingly being reported in routine clinical practice (2).

title: Advanced Cardiovascular‐Kidney‐Metabolic Risk and Risk‐Factor Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Without Established Cardiovascular Disease
creator: Hai Nguyen Ngoc Dang, The Trung Le, Anh Kiem Pham, Linh Duy Le, Nam Van Duc Nguyen, Thanh Thien Tran, Thinh Ba Le, Ny Ha Tuyet Le, Nam Van Le, Hau Phuc Tran, Hung Minh Vu, Duong Hung Tran, Bich Ngoc Hoang Thi, Huy Nhu Pham, Hieu Minh Le, Thang Chi Doan, Binh Anh Ho, Tien Anh Hoang, Minh Van Huynh, T
description: BackgroundCardiovascular‐kidney‐metabolic (CKM) risk stratification may identify patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who require more intensive primary prevention, but real‐world data from Vietnam are limited. We aimed to describe advanced CKM risk and risk‐factor control in Vietnamese patients with T2DM without established cardiovascular disease (CVD).MethodsThis multicenter cross‐sectional study enrolled 1436 adults with T2DM without CVD in Vietnam.

title: The effects of lower limb ischaemic preconditioning: a systematic review
creator: Chloe French, Dan Robbins, Marie Gernigon, Dan Gordon
description: Ischaemic preconditioning (IPC) involves the use of repeated occlusions and reperfusions of the peripheral muscle blood supply at a limb. This systematic literature review examines the typical responses in response to the method of application during an IPC applied at the lower limb.

title: MSC C1: A Potential Hub Linking Stromal Plasticity, Immune Regulation, and Patient Survival in Lung Adenocarcinoma
creator: Houlei Wang, Tianle Ma, Chao Jia, Chunhui Ma
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Bone metastasis of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) directly leads to poor prognosis. This study aimed to dissect the stromal landscape of LUAD with bone metastases. Unsupervised clustering of scRNA‐seq data from LUAD patients with bone metastasis identifies stromal subsets. Pseudotime analysis combined with CytoTRACE stemness scoring reconstructs mesenchymal stromal cell (MSC) differentiation trajectories, while CellChat characterizes cell–cell communication networks among MSC subpopulations.

title: Transcriptome Analysis Identifies a Myeloid‐Like Signature in Relapsed or Refractory B‐Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia Patients With Poor Response to CD19 Chimeric Antigen Receptor T Cell Therapy
creator: Shisen Wang, Wenbing Liu, Ying Wang, Yingxi Xu, Haiyan Xing, Kejing Tang, Zheng Tian, Qing Rao, Shaowei Qiu, Hui Wei, Runxia Gu, Min Wang, Jianxiang Wang
description: BackgroundRelapsed or refractory B‐cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (R/R B‐ALL) patients exhibit heterogeneous responses to CD19 chimeric antigen receptor T‐cell (CAR‐T) therapy. However, current studies primarily focus on the CAR‐T cells or the leukemia blasts, and the patient's intrinsic molecular characteristics before treatment remain poorly understood.

title: Prevalence and determinants of ideal cardiovascular health by sex and region—a population-based study in Peru
creator: Víctor Juan Vera-Ponce, Fiorella E. Zuzunaga-Montoya, Luisa Erika Milagros Vásquez-Romero, Joan A. Loayza-Castro, Eder Jesús Orihuela Manrique, Mario J. Valladares-Garrido, Carmen Inés Gutierrez De Carrillo
description: IntroductionAttaining what the American Heart Association terms Ideal Cardiovascular Health (ICVH) is viewed as an essential objective for preventing cardiovascular diseases (CVD).ObjectiveTo determine the prevalence of ICVH, stratified by sex and region and its associated factors in the adult population of Peru.Materials and methodsAnalytical cross-sectional study. Data were obtained from the Life Stage Food and Nutrition Surveillance Survey (VIANEV).

title: Low‐Dose Nivolumab in Various Cancers: A Real‐World Exploratory Analysis in Resource‐Constrained Settings
creator: Subhas Pandit, Simit Sapkota, Abish Adhikari, Jeebana Bhandari, Sunil Shrestha, Rajani Jha, Gerim Prasai, Anjani Kr Jha
description: BackgroundImmune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), including nivolumab, have significantly improved cancer care. However, due to high costs, there is a significant financial barrier to their widespread access. Emerging evidence shows biological plausibility as well as efficacy of low‐dose nivolumab across different cancers.

title: Why do lactic acid bacteria thrive in chain elongation microbiomes?
creator: Barbara Ulčar, Alberte Regueira, Maja Podojsteršek, Nico Boon, Ramon Ganigué
description: Efficient waste management is necessary to transition towards a more sustainable society. An emerging trend is to use mixed culture biotechnology to produce chemicals from organic waste. Insights into the metabolic interactions between community members and their growth characterization are needed to mediate knowledge-driven bioprocess development and optimization.

title: Sustained induction of PMOS‐like phenotype in mice exposed to letrozole in drinking water
creator: Kennedy A Stevenson, Romy Kerbus, Greg M Anderson, Caroline Decourt
description: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS; formerly polycystic ovary syndrome) is the most common endocrinopathy affecting women of reproductive age, characterized by ovarian dysfunction and hyperandrogenism, with metabolic disturbances including insulin resistance and obesity also present for 50% of PMOS patients. Effective preclinical models are crucial for evaluating therapeutic interventions.

title: Editorial: Promoting nervous system regeneration by treatments targeting neuron-glia interactions
creator: Silmara De Lima, Bruno Siqueira Mietto, Vinicius Toledo Ribas, Victor Tulio Ribeiro-Resende, Alexandre Leite Rodrigues Oliveira, Kevin K. Park
description: al function?” As it seems to happen, the nervous system presents major obstacles and tissue-related characteristics, with regards to its regenerative capacity. While some repair can spontaneously occur after peripheral nervous system (PNS) injury, the regenerative capacity of the central nervous system (CNS) is limited.

title: The Fleming Fund: Key Features of Design and Approach to Strengthening Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance in Low- and Middle-Income Countries
creator: Tim Shorten, Jemima Clarke, Archibald Drake, Ankur Gupta-Wright, Milena von und zur Mühlen, Evelyn Wesangula
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This paper examines the Fleming Fund as a major long-term investment in strengthening antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance in low- and middle-income countries. Established by the UK Department of Health and Social Care in 2015, the Fund committed up to £498 million to support surveillance capacity across 25 countries in Africa and Asia through a One Health approach spanning human, animal and environmental health.

title: Non-destructive real-time analysis of plant metabolite accumulation in radish microgreens under different LED light recipes
creator: Marco Garegnani, Carla Sandri, Claudia Pacelli, Francesca Ferranti, Elisabetta Bennici, Angiola Desiderio, Luca Nardi, Maria Elena Villani
description: IntroductionThe future of human space missions relies on the ability to provide adequate food resources for astronauts and also to reduce stress due to the environment (microgravity and cosmic radiation). In this context, microgreens have been proposed for the astronaut diet because of their fast-growing time and their high levels of bioactive compounds and nutrients (vitamins, antioxidants, minerals, etc.

title: Generating Actionable Data From Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance: Insights From the Fleming Fund's International Experience
creator: Ankur Gupta-Wright, Suliat Yetunde Adeleke, Victoria Adetunji, Qadeer Ahsan, Ritu Amatya, Ben Amos, Brian Asare, Sorie I O Bangura, Cyril Buhler, Nicholas Feasey, N Claire Gordon, Heidi Hopkins, Freddy Eric Kitutu, Toby Leslie, Ibrahima Lo, Seynabou Lo, Ayodele Majekodunmi, Rebecca Maudling, Ntombi
description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a major global health threat, with the greatest burden falling on low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) also challenged with limited surveillance capacity. The UK Government's Fleming Fund was established in 2015 to strengthen AMR surveillance across Africa and Asia through a One Health approach.

title: Weed detection in soybean fields using improved YOLOv7 and evaluating herbicide reduction efficacy
creator: Jinyang Li, Wei Zhang, Hong Zhou, Chuntao Yu, Qingda Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). With the increasing environmental awareness and the demand for sustainable agriculture, herbicide reduction has become an important goal. Accurate and efficient weed detection in soybean fields is the key to test the effectiveness of herbicide application, but current technologies and methods still have some problems in terms of accuracy and efficiency, such as relying on manual detection and poor adaptability to some complex environments.

title: Efficacy of Saffron as an Adjunct to Methylphenidate in Treating ADHD in Children Aged 6–12: A Randomized Clinical Trial
creator: Asieh Hosseinpourfardi, Seyyed Mohammad Saeid Sahaf, Fahimeh Afzaljavan, Atefeh Soltanifar, Fatemeh Moharreri
description: IntroductionAttention‐deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is a common childhood disorder often managed with stimulant medications such as methylphenidate. Around 30% of patients with ADHD do not respond to treatment or cannot tolerate its side effects, which necessitates the consideration of alternative options.

title: Written discourse in diagnosis for acquired neurogenic communication disorders: current evidence and future directions
creator: Hana Kim, Jessica Obermeyer, Robert W. Wiley
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). PurposeWe aimed to perform the first review of research focusing on written discourse performance in people with acquired neurogenic communication disorders. In studies from 2000 onward, we specifically sought to determine: (1) the differences between patient populations and control groups, (2) the differences between different patient populations, (3) longitudinal differences between patient populations, and (4) modality differences between spoken and written discourse performance.MethodsWe completed a thorough search on MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, APAPsycinfo, Web of Science, and Scopus databases.

title: Initial Treatment for Acute Low Back Pain and Risk of Opioid Use Disorder and Overdose
creator: Lisa V. Doan, Anton M. Hung, Mark Olfson, Nicholas T. Williams, Kara E. Rudolph
description: ImportanceGuideline-discordant care for acute low back pain (aLBP) is common and has been associated with adverse outcomes.ObjectivesTo estimate the incidence of new opioid use disorder (OUD) or overdose diagnosis among opioid-naive patients with Medicaid coverage initiating treatment for aLBP and to evaluate the association between initial treatment modalities and subsequent risk of OUD or overdose diagnosis.

title: Human Bone Morphogenetic Protein‐3 Mature Ligand Is Larger Than Recorded Indicating Earlier Publications Are Flawed
creator: David E. Phelan, Caitriona Scaife, Emma R. Dorris, John Russell, Madeline Murphy
description: Bone morphogenetic protein (BMP)‐3 (osteogenin) is an important regulatory cytokine during development and acts as a tumor suppressor in several cancers. BMPs are synthesized as proproteins that are cleaved by proprotein convertases to release biologically active ligands. The BMP‐3 mature ligand is recorded as 16 kDa consisting of carboxy‐terminal Q363‐R472 (110 amino acids).

title: Highly effective viral RdRP translocation hindrance by the remdesivir nucleotide
creator: Rui Li, Qiang Shao, Meihua Wang, Chunyan Feng, Qin Xu, Qisheng Wang, Luqing Shang, Yechun Xu, Peng Gong
description: Nucleoside/nucleotide analogs (NAs) typically interfere with substrate selection and catalysis steps of polymerase nucleotide addition cycle (NAC), thereby affecting polymerase catalytic efficiency. In contrast, their interference with post-chemistry translocation is rarely considered in rational design, partly due to a lack of direct and quantitative evidence for such interference.

title: When, where, and why should we look for vestibular dysfunction in people with diabetes mellitus?
creator: Frank E. DiLiberto, Heather E. R. Kamath, Maxine L. Olson, Marcello Cherchi, Janet O. Helminski, Michael C. Schubert
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The biochemistry of diabetes mellitus results in multi-system tissue compromise that reduces functional mobility and interferes with disease management. Sensory system compromise, such as peripheral neuropathy and retinopathy, are specific examples of tissue compromise detrimental to functional mobility. There is lack of clarity regarding if, when, and where parallel changes in the peripheral vestibular system, an additional essential sensory system for functional mobility, occur as a result of diabetes.

title: Exploring the bistable equilibrium of methylated CpG DNA recognition by the MBD2 protein
creator: Senta Volkenandt, Julia Belyaeva, Torry Li, Matthias Elgeti, Ralf Metzler, Petra Imhof, David C Williams, Mahdi Bagherpoor Helabad
description: Methyl-CpG binding domain 2 (MBD2) is a critical epigenetic regulator that selectively binds methylated CpG dinucleotides, key marks controlling gene regulation and chromatin organization. Understanding the interactions and conformational dynamics underlying this high selectivity is essential to elucidate MBD2’s regulatory role. Here, using extensive classical MD simulations, we explored the formation of the MBD2–mCpG recognition complex.

title: Construction of an anaplastic thyroid cancer stratification signature to guide immune therapy selection and validation of the pivotal gene HLF through in vitro experiments
creator: Li Pengping, Yin Kexin, Xie Yuwei, Sun Ke, Li Rongguo, Wang Zhenyu, Jin Haigang, Wang Shaowen, Huang Yuqing
description: IntroductionWhile most thyroid cancer patients have a favorable prognosis, anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC) remains a particularly aggressive form with a median survival time of just five months. Conventional therapies offer limited benefits for this type of thyroid cancer. Our study aims to identify ATC patients who might bene t from immunotherapy.MethodsOur study uses multiple algorithms by R4.2.

title: Bitter 2,5‐Diketopiperazines From Cocoa Activate Human Bitter Taste Receptors
creator: Silvia Schaefer, Adolfo Luna, Maik Behrens
description: The human taste system enables a rapid analysis of nutritional and non‐nutritional food constituents. Although a bitter taste is considered a warning signal against ingesting potentially harmful substances, not all bitter substances are toxic, and a moderate bitterness is frequently tolerated or even preferred.

title: Remediating cognitive inflexibility in obsessive compulsive disorder and anorexia nervosa neither moderates nor mediates treatment effects: an exploratory study
creator: Boris van Passel, Unna N. Danner, Alexandra E. Dingemans, Theo G. Broekman, Lot C. Sternheim, Eni S. Becker, Annemarie A. van Elburg, Eric F. van Furth, Gert-Jan Hendriks, Daniëlle C. Cath
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveObsessive compulsive disorder (OCD) and anorexia nervosa (AN) are conditions associated with poor cognitive flexibility, a factor considered to interfere with treatment, but research into the relationship between cognitive flexibility and treatment outcome is limited.

title: Whole‐Food Protein Sources Differentially Modulate Postprandial Plasma Dileucine Profiles in the Post‐Exercise State
creator: Žan Zupančič, Geoffrey M Provenzano, Calvin Chen, Gena L Irwin, Alexander V Ulanov, Nicholas A Burd
description: Dileucine, a leucine‐containing dipeptide, may enhance anabolic signaling more than leucine alone. This study examined postprandial plasma dileucine and leucine concentrations after ingesting animal‐ and plant‐ whole foods and their association with muscle protein synthesis rates (MPS). Secondary analysis was performed on plasma samples collected from two randomized controlled trials totaling 26 healthy adults (25 ± 4.3 y).

title: The value of privacy for people with dementia
creator: Eike Buhr, Mark Schweda
description: IntroductionThe concept of privacy marks an astonishing gap in the discussion about care for people with dementia (PwD). In general, questions of privacy play an important role and attract much attention in the ethics of nursing care. Yet, when it comes to dementia care, there is hardly any systematic ethical debate on the topic at all.

title: An App‐Based Proton Pump Inhibitor Discontinuation Tool: A Multicentre, Open‐Label, Randomised Superiority Trial
creator: Lieke M Koggel, Thomas Timmers, Marten A Lantinga, Rudolf B Kool, Cornelis Kramers, Noortje van Herwaarden, Peter D Siersema, SUPPORT study consortium
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundProton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are frequently used without long‐term indication. Discontinuation remains challenging because of rebound symptoms. Whether digital guidance tools improve discontinuation is unknown. We evaluated whether an app improves PPI discontinuation.MethodsIn this open‐label adaptive randomised controlled superiority trial, adults using daily PPI for ≥ 4 weeks without chronic PPI indication, according to the Dutch College of General Practitioners guideline, were recruited from outpatient clinics of Internal Medicine, Gastroenterology, Rheumatology and Nephrology departments at three Dutch hospitals.

title: Corrections to “Cognitive Reserve and Psychological Well‐Being in Aging Population of Community‐Dwellers in Spain”
creator: Unknown
description:
iology, Universidad de Zaragoza, Teruel, Spain (previously listed as 3).

Additionally, an inadvertently omitted funding source has been added to the Funding section. The corrected funding statement should read:

We apologize for these errors.

title: Research on detection methods of related substances and degradation products of the antitumor drug selpercatinib
creator: Jingjing Xiang, Liangliang Cai, Qin Wang, Yonghong Zhu, Yong Han
description: BackgroundSelpercatinib, a selective RET kinase inhibitor, is approved for treating various cancers with RET gene mutations such as RET-rearranged thyroid cancer and non-small cell lung cancer. The presence of process-related and degradation impurities in its active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) can significantly affect its safety and effectiveness. However, research on detecting these impurities is limited.

title: Ferroptosis: a dual-edged sword in tumour growth
creator: Xiangye Zhao, Xiaoning Li, Yinghui Xu
description: Ferroptosis, a recently identified form of non-apoptotic cell death, is distinguished by its dependence on iron-triggered lipid peroxidation and accumulation of iron. It has been linked to various disorders, including the development of tumours. Interestingly, ferroptosis appears to exhibit a dual role in the context of tumour growth.

title: Paradoxical energetics in the polar diatom Fragilariopsis cylindrus exposed to extreme low light
creator: Arthur Plassart, Nathalie Joli, Sneha Sivaram, Sébastien Guérin, Flavienne Bruyant, Marie-Hélène Forget, Chris Bowler, Marcel Babin
description: It is generally considered that Arctic diatoms endure total darkness during polar winters by shifting to a hypometabolic state based on internal reserve mobilization. They can nonetheless rapidly initiate under-ice blooms at extreme low-light levels in early spring. The limits and mechanisms underlying this ability remain unknown.

title: The future of sleep apnea management: we can either ride the bus or drive it
creator: Stephen D. Pittman, Barry Chase, Daniel J. Gottlieb, Dennis Hwang, Douglas B. Kirsch, Neomi A. Shah, Kimberly L. Sterling, Keith Thornton, Teresa R. Barnes, John Tosi, Kelly A. Carden, Richard K. Bogan, Amir Reuveny, Sonia Ancoli-Israel, Atul Malhotra
description: This consensus conference report summarizes discussions on sleep apnea care and management. Our goal is to simplify the journey to optimize success for individuals at risk of obstructive sleep apnea and to facilitate diagnostics, monitoring and communication among the entire healthcare team including patients, primary care physicians, sleep specialists, sleep dentists and other key providers.

title: Association of Cognitive Function With Event‐Related Potentials and Immune Inflammation in Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder
creator: Lu Yang, Liemin Ruan, Zhongze Lou, Zhenglai Liu, Yiqin Huang, Li Zhang, Yunxin Ji
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to investigate cognitive function changes in adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD) and examine their associations with depression severity, event‐related potentials (ERP), T lymphocyte subsets, and inflammatory cytokines to identify exploratory clinical and biological correlates for cognitive impairment in this population.MethodsWe enrolled 89 adolescent patients with MDD and 30 healthy controls, matched for age and gender.

title: Valid Inference for Two Sample Summary Statistics Mendelian Randomization
creator: Kai Wang, Grace Z. Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mendelian randomization (MR) studies increasingly rely on summary statistics from genome‐wide association studies (GWASs). However, current summary‐data methods treat marginal GWAS effect estimates as independent across instrumental single‐nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs), which holds only when the SNPs have no effect. Without imposing this independence assumption, we derive expressions for the two‐stage least squares (TSLS), two‐sample TSLS (TSTSLS), and generalized method‐of‐moments estimators together with their variance estimators using only GWAS summary statistics, assuming the instrumental SNPs are in linkage equilibrium.

title: Variations in Soil Microbiome Assembly Determine Hatching Induction of the Carrot Cyst Nematode Heterodera carotae
creator: Marine Biget, Nathan Vannier, Kévin Gazengel, Bruno Marquer, Juliette Linglin, Christophe Langrume, Catherine Porte, Sylvain Chéreau, Didier Fouville, Sylvain Fournet, Lionel Lebreton, Josselin Montarry
description: Plants shape their microbiota through root exudation to resist environmental constraints. These plant's exuded metabolites also serve as hatching signals for cyst nematodes, a major crop pest, to trigger their parasitic cycle. The “suicide hatching” strategy takes advantage of these exudates as a decoy, inducing hatching of juveniles in the absence of the host plant.

title: Association between Healthy Eating Index-2015 total and metabolic associated fatty liver disease in Americans: a cross-sectional study with U.S. National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey
creator: Genzhong Xu, Ermin Ma, Weitao Zhang, Bo Feng
description: BackgroundUtilizing the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) dataset to investigate the relationship between dietary quality, as assessed by the Healthy Eating Index-2015 (HEI-2015), and the prevalence of metabolic associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) among adults in the United States, our analysis revealed that an increased dietary quality was significantly correlated with a reduced risk of MAFLD in the

title: Efficient production and characterization of melanin from Thermothelomyces hinnuleus SP1, isolated from the coal mines of Chhattisgarh, India
creator: Shalini Pandey, Vineet Meshram, Hany M. Yehia, Abdulhakeem Alzahrani, Nadeem Akhtar, Arunima Sur
description: In the present study, fungi were isolated and screened from barren land in south-eastern Coalfields limited (SECL) in Chhattisgarh, India. Out of 14 isolated fungi, only three fungal isolates exhibited pigmentation in screening studies. The isolated fungal strain SP1 exhibited the highest pigmentation, which was further utilized for in vivo production, purification, and characterization of melanin pigment.

title: A Nelore Cattle Structural Variant Catalog
